Full-stack research engine · not a quote widget

Institutional-style equity research, built from free, official data.

A Python pipeline that ingests prices, SEC filings, macro series and earnings materials, keeps the objective facts apart from the AI interpretation, and exposes every feature through a REST API and a dark, fast Next.js front end.

$ research NVDA prices yfinance fundamentals Finnhub filings SEC EDGAR ✓ macro FRED ✓ note Gemini ✓

Research report

Fact and interpretation, kept apart

Numbers from APIs and filings are stored as-is. The AI note is labelled, attributed, and instructed never to reference a figure that isn't in the input — template output takes over if no model is reachable.

  • Six metric cards — valuation, growth, profitability, financial health, TTM financials
  • Insider transactions parsed from raw Form 4 XML: name, role, buy / sell, size, date
  • Earnings guidance pulled from the 8-K — the legal boilerplate is trimmed first, so the forward outlook survives the token budget
  • Embedded TradingView chart, PDF export, one-click regenerate
Under the hood

One request, a seven-step pipeline

Every ticker lookup runs the same ordered workflow. Each step fails gracefully — a missing source returns a note, never a broken report — and results are cached in Postgres, so a repeat lookup is free.

  1. 1Price history & stats
  2. 2Fundamentals
  3. 3Peer comparison
  4. 4SEC insider activity
  5. 5Transcript + AI read
  6. 6Analyst consensus & macro
  7. 7AI research note

Portfolio

Positions, risk, and an honest backtest

Postgres-backed positions with live P&L and weights, a sector donut, and a performance line that says exactly what it measures.

  • Correlation-based risk contribution and scenario analysis — −20% market, rates +100 bps
  • Performance against a benchmark of your choice: SPY, QQQ, SOXX, VTI
  • The chart is a backtest of current holdings, and the panel says so — not a fabricated account history
Weekly brief

Grounded in this week's news, not a recap of weights

The brief receives the macro snapshot, each holding's recent move, and real dated headlines. The prompt bans restating portfolio weights as if they were insight.

  • Every market claim traces to a headline in the input — publisher and date cited inline
  • On Gemini it also runs live Google Search grounding
  • Context → what moved and why → risks with real catalysts → bottom line
Alerts

Metric rules, checked against the live pipeline

Price, P/E, revenue-growth or insider-filing thresholds. The list loads instantly; the condition check runs in the background and fills in the status in place.

  • A lightweight price fetch handles price rules — sub-second, no full pipeline run
  • Triggered state surfaces as a chip, so what needs attention reads at a glance
Macro calendar

The week's data releases, in context

A dedicated view of upcoming US economic events — the releases the weekly brief keeps naming as near-term risks.

  • Actual vs. forecast for ISM, JOLTS, non-farm payrolls, CPI and more
  • Display-only: the numbers the pipeline uses still come from FRED
